Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.3 is the brother of deceased Nakka Praveen who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 12.09.2022 due to the negligence of the driver of the respondent's car.

It is submitted that on 12.09.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., deceased N a k k a P r a v e e n w a s r i d i n g H o n d a U n i c o r n m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g Reg.No.AP-39-BB-7396 slowly, carefully and cautiously by following traffic rules on Piler - Kadapa road, near Ponthalacheruvu cross, Piler Mandal, Annamayya District,
Andhra Pradesh, at that time, the respondent's Toyota Etios GD car bearing Nakka Aparna vs Sake Anand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123688969/
2 Reg.No.AP-39-HR-5087 which was driven by its driver rashly and negligently with high speed, endangering to human life SCCH 15 4 MVC No.5046/2022 and dashed against the deceased's motor cycle resulting in the accident.
As a result of the collision, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Consequently, on 13.09.2022 a FIR No.257/2022 was registered with the Annamayya Police station under Sec.304(A) of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC against the driver of Respondent No.1 vehicle.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 24 years and working as driver was earning Rs.40,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12%
p.a in the interest of justice and equity.

3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the SCCH 15 5 MVC No.5046/2022 Respondents,
Respondent No.1 has remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that the deceased himself was tort feasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the policy of insurance issued by this respondent subject to the terms and conditions, expectations and limitations.

The age, occupation and the income of the deceased and manner of the accident and vehicle involved in the accident and the cause of death are denied and the petitioners are called upon to prove the same.
It is submitted that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

4. The Respondent No.3 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The present petition is not maintainable either in law or facts.
SCCH 15 6 MVC No.5046/2022 This court has no territorial jurisdiction to try this petition.
The manner of the accident is denied.
The accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased himself and not due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of the bus.

The APSRTC is not at all involved in the accident and hence not a Nakka Aparna vs Sake Anand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123688969/

necessary or proper party.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.3 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 18.07.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. Nakka Praveen S/o Venkatachalapathi was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 12.09.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., on Piler to Kadapa Road, near Ponthalacheruvu cross, Piler Mandal, Annamayya District, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Toyota Etios Car bearing Reg.No.AP-39-HR-5087 by its driver?
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.5046/2022 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Nakka Praveen?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If yes,
what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?

4) What Order or Award?

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
SCCH 15 8 MVC No.5046/2022  REASONS 8
. Issue No.1:
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioners that, petitioner No.3 is examined as PW.1.

In his evidence he has deposed regarding the manner of the accident and stated that on 12.09.2022 at about 8.30 p.m., on Piler - Kadapa road,
near Ponthalacheruvu cross, Piler mandal, Annamayya District, Andhra Pradesh,

deceased Nakka Praveen was proceeding on Honda Unicorn motorcycle bearing Reg.NoAP-39-BB-7396 and was proceeding towards Piler slowly and at that time Toyota Etios GD car bearing Reg.No.AP-39-HR-5087 (herein after offending vehicle)
came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased and Nakka Praveen succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

In support of the said testimony petitioners have produced Ex.P1 - FIR registered on the basis of the complaint - Ex.P2 given against the driver of the offending vehicle and Ex.P3- IMV report discloses that the front portion of the motorcycle as well as the car has been damaged in the accident.

Ex.P7 - charge sheet filed after investigation, wherein the PSI has filed charge sheet against the driver of Etios Car as well as the driver of APSRTC bus SCCH 15 9 MVC No.5046/2022 bearing Reg.No.AP-03-Z-5149 and APSRTC bus subsequently arraigned as Respondent No.3 in this case.

9. As far as the rash and negligent driving is concerned respondent No.3 has submitted that accident did not took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus of respondent No.3 and hence respondent No.3 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
10. As far as the rashness and negligence is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by learned counsel for respondent No.2 and respondent No.3

in the cross-examination of PW.1 by counsel for respondent No.2 has taken contention that there is curve at the road and the junction at distance of 300 meters from the curve and there is no divider on the road.

The contention taken is that in the charge sheet the APSRTC bus driver is also accused No.2 and the deceased himself rode in a rash and negligent manner and knocked by the bus resulting in the accident.

However in the entire cross-examination respondent No.2 has not denied the involvement of Etios car in the accident and has not seriously disputed that accident has been caused due to the rash and SCCH 15 10 MVC No.5046/2022 negligent driving of driver of Etios Car.

As far as involvement of APSRTC bus in the accident is concerned on the perusal of the charge sheet it is crystal clear that the bus is not involved in the accident and it has only subsequently collided with the car and caused damage to the car.

In the charge sheet it has been clearly mentioned that the car came from the opposite side i.e., Piler side to Kadapa side in a rash and negligent manner overtaking another vehicle lost control and hit against the motorcycle of the deceased Praveen.

It is further stated that deceased Nakka Praveen fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot and in the meanwhile respondent No.3 bus drove in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the offending vehicle/car causing damages to the front portion of the car.

These aspects clearly disclose that it is only subsequently after the accident that the bus collided with the car and hence as far as this case is concerned there is no involvement of respondent No.3 bus.
In addition in the cross- examination of PW.1 also he has clearly stated that they have not made any claim against the respondent No.3.

Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence it is satisfactorily established that SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5046/2022 the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Etios car and not due to the fault of APSRTC bus driver.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative ".

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the, mother, father and brother of the deceased Nakka Praveen.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P8 to 11 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 to 3 and the deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

12. In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

entities.text: Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Reliance can also be placed on the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for SCCH 15 12 MVC No.5046/2022 compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."
13. Though the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and petitioner No.3 is the brother of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Nakka Praveen have a right to apply for compensation.

sentences.text: As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Nakka Praveen and also they have proved that the death of the Nakka Praveen has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 24 years.
Ex.P-11 is the Aadhaar card SCCH 15 13 MVC No.5046/2022 which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 15.08.1998.
The alleged accident has taken place on 12.09.2022.
Hence, by considering Ex.P11, the age of the deceased is taken as 24 years.
15. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working as a driver and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence or adduced the evidence of the employer or any salary payment receipts to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,500X 12= 1,86,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,86,000/-.
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

sentences.text: The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.5046/2022 age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the Nakka Aparna vs Sake Anand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123688969/
7 deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.

sentences.text: 17. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his parents and sibling.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra), since the SCCH 15 16 MVC No.5046/2022 deceased was a bachelor, the deductions towards the personal expenses would be 1/2.
18.
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.15,500/- comes to Rs.6,200/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.21,700/- p.m. (Rs.15,500/- + Rs.6,200/- =
Rs.21,700/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 18.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that, if the deceased was bachelor, half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

19. After deducting half of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.21,700/- it comes to Rs.10,850/- (21,700/- - 10,850/-) and multiplier applied is 18, (Rs.10,850/- x 12 = 1,30,200/-,
Rs.1,30,200/- x 18 = 23,43,600/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,43,600/- towards loss of dependency.

SCCH 15 17 MVC No.5046/2022 Medical expenses:
The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
20. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to SCCH 15 18 MVC No.5046/2022 Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Toyota Etios GD car bearing Reg.No.AP-39-HR-5087.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

22. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest SCCH 15 20 MVC No.5046/2022 is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT. LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

23. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,25,100/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As far as involvement of APSRTC bus in the accident is concerned on the perusal of the charge sheet it is crystal clear that the bus is not involved in the accident and it has only subsequently collided with the car and caused damage to the car.
These aspects clearly disclose that it is only subsequently after the accident that the bus collided with the car and hence as far as this case is concerned there is no involvement of respondent No.3 bus.
In addition in the cross- examination of PW.1 also he has clearly stated that they have not made any claim against the respondent No.3.
Hence, in the absence of any rebuttal evidence it is satisfactorily established that SCCH 15 11 MVC No.5046/2022 the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Etios car and not due to the fault of APSRTC bus driver.
12. In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence or adduced the evidence of the employer or any salary payment receipts to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 15,500X 12= 1,86,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of Claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,86,000/-.
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.
The issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.
If these determinants are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in these decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."
Moving forward with the issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the Nakka Aparna vs Sake Anand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123688969/
7 deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.
